prompt: What is OSIsoft's first AF commandment?

options.text: Thou shalt use Templates
Thou shalt use the default %Server%
Thou shalt model everything at once
Thou shalt store relational data in AF attributes

explanation: "Thou shalt use Templates": build every element from a template, even an empty one. The default %Server% and storing relational data in AF are things OSIsoft advises against.

prompt: Which design lets you repoint all of them by editing one value?

options.text: Server path set to %@\Data Archive|Name% and tag name to %@.|TagName%, so one Data Archive Name attribute drives them
Keep the default %Server% and rename PRODPI01 to DEVPI01
Edit each attribute by hand after the move
Use Allow Extensions on every element

scenario: Your AF database has 4,000 PI Point attributes pointing at the development Data Archive DEVPI01. Next month it moves to production server PRODPI01.
explanation: AVEVA's easy wins recommend substitution parameters pointing at an explicit configuration attribute; editing one Data Archive Name attribute repoints all linked attributes. Relying on the default %Server% is specifically discouraged.

prompt: A PI Vision display shows a 90-day average using a PI Point data reference Value Retrieval Method, and it is slow. What does AVEVA recommend?

options.text: Move the calculation to Asset Analytics and store the result in a PI Point
Increase ArcMaxCollect
Convert it to a Formula data reference
Enable Allow Extensions

explanation: Value Retrieval Methods are computed on the fly by the Data Archive each time they are read; move them to Asset Analytics. Formula chains have the same problem, so converting to a Formula does not help.

prompt: Some pumps need three extra attributes. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: A derived template that adds the attributes, with Allow Extensions disabled on the base template
Turn on Allow Extensions on the base template and add attributes per element
Build those pumps without a template
Add the attributes to the Configuration database

explanation: Prefer derived templates for subsets of assets and disable Allow Extensions on base templates, because extensions "will no longer guarantee all elements have the same set of attributes."

prompt: As a rule of thumb, import no more than about how many rows into a (non-external) AF table?
explanation: The rule of thumb is about 10,000 rows, because non-external tables are loaded entirely into client memory. Use parameterised queries on external tables for more.

prompt: Backfilling 6 months with a 1-minute trigger gives about how many evaluations, compared with 180 for a daily trigger?
explanation: 180 days x 1,440 minutes = 259,200 evaluations. AVEVA uses this example to argue for scheduling by need.

prompt: Why should you disable analyses that are in Warning or Error state?

options.text: PI Analysis Service retries them every 15 minutes
They delete their output tags
They lock the AF database
They block check-in

explanation: Analyses enabled before they are configured correctly are retried by PI Analysis Service every 15 minutes, which wastes resources.

prompt: Which of these are AF anti-patterns according to OSIsoft and AVEVA? Select all that apply.

options.text: Free-text values where an enumeration set would control them
Copy-paste data references that point at another element's tag
A Formula with a hard-coded unit count for an aggregate
Using a Rollup analysis for aggregates
Hiding helper attributes such as TagName

explanation: Free-text typos caused NoData, copy-paste references pointed at FFS03's point, and hard-coded formulas fail when an element is deleted. Rollup analyses and hiding helper attributes are recommended practices.

prompt: True or false: AFImport from a master AF database propagates deletions to the site databases.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. Imports do not propagate deletions; to match, you delete everything and recreate it (then update data references), or use the AF SDK.

prompt: Why does the AF course recommend fewer, larger AF databases organised by business unit rather than by plant?

options.text: AF references only work within one database
Each AF database needs its own SQL Server
PI Vision can open only one database
Smaller databases cannot use templates

explanation: AF references only work within one database, so splitting by plant breaks cross-plant references. The course also says not to organise assets in the Configuration database.

prompt: Put the AF design approach the course recommends in order.

items.text: Add extra views with element references for other audiences

explanation: Design top-down, then build bottom-up; bottom-up alone "lacks vision" and top-down alone can "drift away from reality". Extra views come from element references once the main hierarchy exists.

prompt: Match each AF problem to AVEVA's recommended fix.

pairs.left: Copy-paste data reference pointing at the wrong element
Whole external table loaded for each lookup

explanation: These are the easy wins: Reset to Template fixes copied references; enumeration sets control values; parameterised queries select on the server; expression variables avoid repeated calculations (1.6 ms to 0.6 ms in the example).
